# Syntakt: agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-21, research snapshot `ac55c65383b3`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

Full version. The brief one is [syntakt-brief.md](syntakt-brief.md).

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc] [hw]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [doc] [emu] [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [emu] [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]
- **A65** Judge a load budget by the playing load and include the new module's own cost. [hw]
- **A66** On a DSP that waits on a second core, put long work at the end of the frame, not at its head. [hw]
- **A67** Never raise a note's trig and its end in the same audio block. [hw]
- **A68** Before a software reset, anything the next boot must read has to be in RAM, not only in the cache. [hw]
- **A69** Take the stock bytes a run-time patch replays from a copy made before the OS and the flashed build ran, never from live RAM. [emu]
- **A70** Never land a change on the tick a stock event is due and rely on a tie between its time and the clock. [hw]
- **A71** Write at most one value per track, step and parameter in one change. [emu]
- **A72** When you extend a stock table that a setting indexes, extend every table that setting indexes, including tables the OS builds in RAM at run time. [hw]
- **A73** A neutral setting of an effect must give back stock's routing, not only a flat response. [hw]
- **A74** Build mod code with undefined-behaviour warnings as errors, at least `-Werror=return-type`. [emu]
- **A75** On the Model:Cycles, an added machine whose oscillator runs on through a trig must keep the stock VCA from cutting at the trig. [hw]
- **A76** Syntakt: never write SPI NOR `0x300000-0x380000`, and keep the OS container under 2 MB. [doc]
- **A77** Before you store mod data in a byte of a stock record, find every stock routine that reads or writes it, and test with a project that uses every feature of that record. [hw]
- **A78** When a base keeps its own data inside a stock record, shrink the core's area by the same bytes and refuse an overlap at build time. [hw]
- **A79** Test every edit path on a pattern, bank and project far from the defaults, not only on A01. [hw]
- **A80** A parameter a mod sets right before it plays a note may be smoothed by the OS: set the smoothing state too, or set the value a few blocks earlier, and listen on a unit. [hw]
- **A81** A sound a mod starts without a trig must obey the track's mute itself. [?]
- **A82** On the Octatrack, read the Part a track is playing from stock's per-track pair (`0x8000182a` / `0x80001832` + t), not from the UI or engine Part. [hw]
- **A83** Test the smallest legal build as well as the full one. [hw]
- **A84** When you patch a stock routine for audio tracks, find its MIDI-track twin and patch and test that too. [hw]
- **A85** A mod machine that stock sees as another machine must handle both edges of a machine switch itself. [hw]
- **A86** Take key ids from the target device's own decoder table, never from another model. [emu] [hw]
- **A87** Place card data by the smallest capacity the firmware accepts, and check the capacity the driver reports before you touch the card. [hw]
- **A88** When a mod changes the USB descriptors at run time, bring the controller back from a context that keeps running, check that it attached, and keep every other host client off the device while it reconnects. [hw]
- **A89** On the Octatrack, do not change which effects the DSP holds while a project loads; plan only from the complete effect map. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Syntakt

- **C8** (C) Give every check a control that fails when the checker is broken. dnfw's LFO4 bridge passed every check and then faulted on a Digitone II. Three checks had reported success about work they never did: snapshot harnesses cleared code that no real boot had run; a boot gate printed "Safe to flash" after an unrelated edit had deleted its coverage section; and an emulator call returned 0 for a value that was present. Use a key nothing set that must read back absent, a routine list that must not be empty, a coverage line that must appear. A green result from an untested instrument is not evidence. `[hw]` {dn2-lfo4} Incidents: [I42](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i42-checks-reported-success-about-work-they-never-did). Test a safety mechanism's first step end to end through the production code: Synfact's safe-boot trial passed unit tests that replaced the eMMC write with a double, then crashed every boot on a Syntakt because the real table had no write function. Incidents: [I62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i62-a-safe-boot-trial-crashed-every-boot), [I56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit). For UI lifecycle tests, replay the actual edit and its notifications without manually repairing the next view. Armio's sampler tests explicitly reselected SYN before turning the sample knob; that hid a Machine-change path which left the old view attached. The corrected replay fails on R020 and passes the R021/R022 fix. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incident: [I51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i51-the-sample-popup-did-not-open-after-switching-machines). Run view opening and closing through the native push, compose, tick and cleanup, not through doubles: on the Syntakt a view a mod pushes is composed and ticked before the push returns, and stock's deferred cleanup can drop a close raised then, so Synfact's ARP pages stayed blank on the unit while stubbed tests passed. Publish a view's state before you push it. `[hw]` {synfact-1117} Incident: [I115](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i115-arp-pages-stayed-blank-or-lost-their-keys-after-permanent-mute-syntakt).
- **E5** (E) Test incremental working-state persistence separately from SAVE PROJECT. A mod's companion can pass explicit save/reload while remaining stale in the unsaved working backup. On DN2 1.11, native settings updates bypass the whole-project serializer; armio's sample extension missed that path. Exercise load, change and unload through real notifications, serialize the working backup, then restore into a fresh emulator without retaining its heap. Keep current-project ownership/UID checks and the same lock as pool mutations; do not replace a saved checkpoint or add storage work to the shutdown interrupt. A passing replay does not prove physical power-loss recovery or that a frozen task completed its queue. `[emu]` {armio-r022} Incidents: [I77](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i77-knob-assignments-a-mod-kept-in-a-kits-spare-bytes-were-lost-at-power-on) (Digitakt mk1: a cold boot after SAVE PROJECT drops kit spare bytes that LOAD PROJECT keeps), [I52](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i52-new-project-samples-were-missing-after-reboot), [I116](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i116-a-step-order-mod-missed-two-readers-of-its-state-syntakt) (Syntakt: a power cycle without a save restores kits from mirror slots that only `KitActive::kitChanged` re-encodes).

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Syntakt (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`): if the OS still boots, flash the stock `.syx` via Transfer's Drop page (works even if a mod misbehaved); if not, MIDI interface with a 5-pin OUT to the Syntakt's MIDI IN ("USB doesn't work from the startup menu"), FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, Transfer SYSEX TRANSFER "OS Upgrade via device startup menu", tens of minutes at 31.25 kbit/s, the unit restarts itself. Avoid TRIG 2 (empty reset) and TRIG 3 (factory reset) in the startup menu - both erase data. Do a dry run of the DIN procedure with the stock OS before the first flash; flash only files for which `tools/unpack/eft.py info <file>` reports `checksums : ok`; no hardware results are reported on the page. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery} (`recovery#2934ea2d`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L36))

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB35** A Data API card write takes its length from the host and is bounded only by the card's end (Syntakt, OS 1.42 (the same eMMC write and erase code is in Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.11/1.12; whether their Data API sizes a write the same way is not read); open in stock). Workaround: a host client must bound the size to the slot; digikit's card guard hooks both entries and refuses a request outside the stock area `[0, 0x180000)` (emulator-tested).

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I20** Mod code at a "free" address crashed projects with certain samples. Cause: mod code at `0x46000000`, memory stock uses for those samples. Fix: v0.8.1 unpacks the mod code into a 64 KB block that a hook at the end of heap init (`0x4010358E`) reserves first. Rules: D11.
- **I50** Mod data written for default settings slowed project load and save. Cause: the ARP mod sealed a 320-byte carrier for every kit even with default settings, so load checked all 1,664 bindings; the project itself was valid. Fix: leave the carrier absent while all thirteen rows are defaults: 81 % fewer emulated instructions for a full serialization. Rules: E4.
- **I62** A safe-boot trial crashed every boot. Cause: the boot's eMMC accessor table had no write function, so marking the bank TRYING called address 0; the record never changed, so every boot retried the same bank. The unit tests had replaced exactly this piece with doubles. Fix: core 1.7.1 adds the write function, storage fails closed on a table without one, and an end-to-end test through the production loader reproduces the crash. Rules: C8.
- **I63** A mod's memory window broke the BASE/WDTH filter. Cause: the stock base-width filter reads Q31 poles from a 508-entry table with a zero tail and indexes up to 1023; Synfact's companion window sat in that tail, so BASE+WDTH of 128 or more read code as poles. Fix: core 1.7.2 bounds the index to 508. Rules: A43.
- **I64** A chorus running from DDR overloaded the Syntakt's MAIN CPU. Cause: all chorus code ran from DDR; about 5.4 KB of code was fetched per block. Fix: 0.2 moved the hot code and kernels into MAIN SRAM (0.2 KB fetched per block). Rules: A34.
- **I104** A development core put its module binder in boot storage that startup wipes. Cause: to free room in the resident reserve, the module binder had been moved into the storage appended after the MAIN image. Startup clears and reuses that storage once the resident copy is done, so the call from the machine loader jumped into wiped memory. The opcode audit and host tests passed because neither modelled the clearing, and the test fixtures filled the event lists directly instead of calling the binder. Fix: core 1.8.1.1 puts the binder and dispatcher back in resident memory; the builder now refuses startup entries that are not resident, and a new emulator test clears the appended storage and reproduces the exception at the same address as a negative control. 1.8.1.1 boots and plays on the unit. A failed bank may stay marked TRYING, so send it again and check the versions in System Info. Rules: A42,C8.
- **I115** ARP pages stayed blank or lost their keys after permanent mute (Syntakt). Cause: several, each hidden by a test double: the opening guard did not know MainScreen's six normal child views; a view pushed by the mod is composed and ticked synchronously before the push returns, so the mod's tick closed its own new view; and stock's deferred view cleanup (`0x40100ea4`) clears its pending flag after the visibility call, losing a close raised by a tick during that call, so a closed view stayed in the list and blocked ARP. Fix: ARP 1.10.4 selects its page before the push; core 1.8.2 clears the flag before the visibility call (same 18-byte window). Tests now run the native push, compose, tick and cleanup instead of stubs. Rules: C8.
- **I116** A step-order mod missed two readers of its state (Syntakt). Cause: the trig LEDs read the step through their own accessor `0x4008b734`, not the patched sequencer sites; and a power cycle without a save restores kits from their mirror slots, which are only re-encoded when `KitActive::kitChanged` (`0x40172250`) runs after a native kit edit. Fix: build 3 patches the accessor as a fifth site; build 10 calls `kitChanged` for the playing kit after each mode change (checked in Unicorn, not yet on the unit). Rules: E5,A31.
- **I139** A neutral filter setting still coloured the mix through the analog FX block (Syntakt Performance Mods). Cause: THRU left the whole mix routed through the analog FX block. Fix: TEST37c makes THRU a full bypass (filter off, stock routing kept, no CPU at THRU). Rules: A73.
- **I145** Many stock samples overwrote Synfact's resident core and crashed it at boot (Synfact). Cause: at boot stock concatenates all 64 stock samples into one blob in MAIN DDR from `0x4584f2c5`; past 84 s of audio in all it runs over the 64 KiB resident core at `0x46000000`. The core's guards checked each slot on disk and parsed the blob only after stock had built it. Reproduced in Unicorn for both OS versions (first overlapping write in stock's memcpy while copying slot 17). Fix: core 2.0.1 no longer calls the stock builder; it streams each sender page from eMMC with 5 KiB of scratch, and draws waveforms on demand. Rules: A34,D11.
- **I171** A third LFO page showed ERR labels when the bank held only modules (Synfact core 2.1.1, Syntakt). Cause: the machine binder returned early for a bank with no machines and never set the registry active. The LFO3 page hooks still ran, but every provider lookup was skipped while the registry was inactive, so LFO3's ids fell through to stock's fallbacks. Every earlier test had at least one machine in the bank. Fix: core 2.1.2 drops the early return; an empty registry gets valid storage before it becomes active. A host regression and a Unicorn test with two module-only banks cover it, with the old core as a negative control. Rules: A83.
- **I181** The digikit MODULES page froze a Syntakt: it used the Digitakt II key ids. Cause: the list page replaces the stock key handler and compared key ids with the Digitakt II values (YES 10, NO 12, RIGHT 15). An empty list passes only NO to the stock handler. On the Syntakt the firmware key index 12 is YES and NO is 13 (decoder table `0x401d7a48`), so NO was swallowed with every other key. Fix: key ids and flag bits per device in the device file (Syntakt YES 12, NO 13, RIGHT 17, LEVEL push 48); an empty list now swallows only YES and RIGHT and passes every other key to the stock handler; the build refuses a device file without the key table. A test compares the ids with the stock decoder table. Rules: A86.
- **I182** The first digikit store on a Syntakt lay beyond the unit's card. Cause: the store reused the Digitone II range (sectors `0x800000-0x2e1a000`, made for the 32 GB part the emulators model), but the unit's eMMC is the 1.82 GiB part (`0x3a4000` sectors, the smallest the firmware's part table lists; the table is not enforced at boot). Fix: a fixed 512 MiB store at `0x200000-0x300000`, above every stock sector (below `0x180000`) and below the smallest listed capacity, checked at boot against the driver's capacity getter; INFO and HEALTH show the capacity. On the unit the new store took uploads, listing and removal, and a content module ran from it. Rules: A87.
- **I183** A full digikit image hung a Syntakt at the logo: the bootstrap's unpack overran its stream. Cause: the Syntakt bootstrap stages packed MAIN at `0x40200000`, not at the `0x40400000` of the Digitakt II and Digitone II, and unpacks it in place with no bound. The full image's stream had an in-place margin of -42,486 bytes at that stage (stock +96,356), so the output overwrote unread stream bytes and the decoder ran away before MAIN started. The emulator installs MAIN directly and never runs that unpack; the device file had copied the Digitakt II stage value; the margin was checked only for the repacked section 7. Fix: the stage is per-device data read from section 2; patchkit writes the stream's last tokens as literals until the margin is at least 8 KiB and refuses an image below that in `verify`, `preflight` and `flash`, printing the margin. The repaired full image boots on the unit. Rules: A14.
- **I46** Syntakt startup-menu recovery tested over DIN. Cause: test. Fix: — Rules: A11,A36.
- **I184** A memory canary held with all 64 sample slots loaded, then trig-seedr passed its first checks (Syntakt). Cause: the project's staged first-flash plan: way back first, a null repack, a memory canary, then the mod. Fix: none needed. Rules: A11,A43.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O1** Syntakt OS signing: A) SyntHack OS: 1.41 carries an HMAC-SHA256, with the key derived from the image B) digikit finding 70: 1.42 has no HMAC trailer; 2026-11-18 {digikit-st-1118}: no trailer slot at all (the container ends at section 8 rounded to 16; a stock rebuild matches byte for byte)
- **O3** Syntakt CPU #1 load: A) ~89 % of the audio interrupt at rest (SyntHack, measured with DTIM0) B) the render is 85.8k of 166.7k cycles per block (SY FM4)
- **O34** Syntakt OS container cap: A) Modwerk: at most 2 MB (the upgrade's receive buffer) {modwerk-st-goal} B) digikit `syntakt.toml`: `container_max = 0x300000`, copied from DT2/DN2 with the Syntakt flash map not read; digikit's own finding 141 puts the analog calibration record at NOR `0x300000` (backup `0x340000`), so a container from `0x80000` longer than `0x280000` would reach it {digikit-st-1118}
- **O35** Top of Syntakt DDR (OS 1.42): A) Modwerk freed `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` by lowering the stack 128 KB (one unit, with a sample reload) {modwerk-st-goal} B) digikit: `0x47c00000-0x48000000` is a 4 MiB ring cleared at boot and written every frame (static) {digikit-st-1118}
- **O36** Syntakt core clock: A) SyntHack: about 250 MHz (166,667 cycles per block) {synthack-docs} B) digikit assumes a 264 MHz core and 132 MHz bus (176,000 cycles per 1500 Hz frame) {digikit-st-1118}
- **O40** Syntakt 128 x 64 screen bitmap bit order (OS 1.42): A) Synfact: the native Bitmap API keeps 256 big-endian words per array, two words a column; y = 0 is bit 31 of the first word, y = 63 bit 0 of the second `[emu]` {synfact-1119} B) trig-seedr: the screen bitmap object `{vtable, 128, 64, 2, pixels}` has its pixels at +16, 8 bytes a column, row 0 at the top in bit 0 of the column's last byte (one pixel measured in analog-emu) {trig-seedr-1120}
- **O41** Syntakt AUDIO (section 7) vector table: A) syntakt.md, digikit peer facts: section 7 builds a 256-entry vector table at `0x4004005c` {digikit-st-1118} B) Synfact AUDIO memory map: VBR is `0x40000000`, the vectors are `0x40000000-0x400003ff`, and `0x4004005c` is the word that holds the VBR value (instructions `0x40000dbe`, `0x40001064`) {synfact-1120}
- **O42** Syntakt stock MAIN instructions per audio block: A) digikit: about 117,000 instructions per frame, MAIN at 264 MHz (189.9 M instructions/s) {digikit-st-1118} B) Synfact: about 72,400 instructions per block (default project in PLAY, exact counts in analog-emu), cost modelled at 250 MHz {synfact-1120}
- **O43** Syntakt AUDIO stack reserve below `0x48000000`: A) SynCrackd: leave the top megabyte for the stack (depth not measured) {syncrackd-mm} B) Synfact core 2.2 keeps only 64 KiB (`0x47feff50-0x48000000`); static stack bound 3,140 bytes; its probe of the real depth has no result yet {synfact-1120}

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H47** (stock) On Syntakt OS 1.42 the top 4 MiB of DDR (`0x47c00000-0x48000000`) is rewritten every frame while delay and reverb are in use, so Modwerk's freed `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` is not free then. Test: Fill `0x47fe0000-0x48000000` and `0x478c0000-0x47bf0000` with a pattern after boot, play a pattern with heavy delay and reverb sends, load a sample-heavy project, then read back. Settles O35. The lower range is done for one unit: trig-seedr's canary over `0x478b0000-0x47bf0000` held with all 64 sample slots loaded (2026-11-19, I184) {trig-seedr-1121}; the top 4 MiB is still open.
- **H48** (stock) Holding TRIG 16 at power-on on a Syntakt with stock OS 1.42 does nothing else than (at most) toggle step 16 of the first pattern; MAIN has no boot-time key reader. Test: Hold TRIG 16 while powering on a stock unit; check the boot and step 16.
- **H60** (stock) A stock Syntakt (OS 1.42) keeps an unsaved trig edit across a power-off once its supercap is charged: the power-off handler writes the working state only when byte `0x43be3154` is set, which happens when PPDSDR_G bit 3 (supercap charged) reads high. Test: Leave the unit on for a few minutes, add a trig without saving, switch off and on: is the trig there? Repeat right after a cold start. Partly seen 2026-11-19: on one unit running trig-seedr (stock save path) an applied and a pending take survived a power off {trig-seedr-1121}; a plain stock unit and a power off right after a cold start are still open.
- **H61** (stock) Syntakt OS 1.42 has no parameter-lock row limit (unlike the Rytm's 72 rows a pattern): each track's lock store is a full 64-step x 71-id matrix and the set routine counts no rows. Test: Lock several SYN, FLTR and AMP parameters on every step of several tracks; look for any refusal.
- **H66** (stock) A Syntakt (OS 1.42) whose MAIN unpack runs away in the bootstrap (I183, a hang at the logo) still reaches the STARTUP menu with FUNC held at power-on, because the bootstrap reads the keys before it copies and unpacks section 3 (read on the DT2 bootstrap, finding 01). Test: Next time a build hangs at the logo: hold FUNC at power-on, choose TRIG 4 and send stock over DIN; report whether the menu came up. Do not provoke the hang for this.
- **H64** (probe) On a Syntakt (OS 1.42) nothing writes AUDIO RAM `0x4404ff50-0x47ff0000` in normal use, and the AUDIO stack stays well under 64 KiB (O43). Test: Run Synfact's HIGH MEM PROBE for several minutes with samplers, FM, POLY, ARP, chorus, the recorder and a project load and save; HIGH BAD must stay 0; read STACK PEAK.
- **T4** (needs unit + SyntHack, effort M) Measure CPU #1 load with the digihealth DMA-timer method over the whole interrupt, at rest and busy
- **T5** (needs files, effort S) Check the trailer and HMAC of 1.40A/1.41/1.42 with your own files (elektron-firmware-tool, digikit)
- **T6** (needs files, effort M) Translate SyntHack/machine-45 anchors from 1.41 to 1.42 (byte patterns, not addresses) (tool: [`scripts/anchor_translate.py`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/scripts/anchor_translate.py), 2026-11-11: you supply both images; it reports per address whether the translation is exact, bracketed, one-sided or ambiguous)
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).

The margin (decompressed minus compressed) must stay below ~`0x1FFC00` at every point of the stream. Stock 1.41 has a margin of +99,938 B. A build padded with zeros to `0x40350000` (-8,751 B) did not boot, tested twice and hung on the logo. Zero padding is the worst case; already-compressed payloads raise the margin. SyntHack refuses builds under 4 KB of margin. `[hw]` — `syntakt#43e5b0cc` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L53) · Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)

- [hw] Where mod code lives at run time (SyntHack modarea, v0.8.1+): The OS image has only ~2 KB free, and everything after it is zeroed at boot. At boot it is unpacked into the first 64 KB block of the OS heap: buddy allocator `0x4010350C`, 16 MB pool at `0x444E38C0`. The block is reserved by a call right after heap initialization, so it always gets index 0, and the OS never hands it out again. - [doc] [emu] How the peer CPU gets its program: MAIN reads ids 6 and 7 from the OS directory in NOR (`0x80000`, "ELE3", 16-byte entries from `0x80020`: id, offset, length) and streams them at every boot over DSPI2 (`0xEC038000`) in slave mode, eDMA channel 29 one byte per request. Buffers are `0xAA | big-endian length | payload`: id 6 at `0x4f8af2c1` after eight `0xFF` bytes (MAIN changes byte 1 from `0x01` to `0x0f`), id 7 at `0x4f84f2c1` (length limit `0x5fffb`, matching SY FM4's "0x60000 - 5"). Section 6 (stage 1, SRAM `0x80000000`) sets up DDR, takes the stream and jumps through `*(0x40000400)`. Who starts DSPI0 as master before stage 1 is open. `[doc]` (stream bytes `[emu]`: payload equals section 7 by SHA-256) — `syntakt#6a9456f9` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:220](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L220) · Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
- [emu] Two pins form the handshake: MAIN's doorbell (GPIO port A bit 4) is the peer's DTIM0 capture event (vector 96); the peer's pin (port 6 bit 2: set via `0xEC09401E`, cleared via `0xEC09402A`) is MAIN's EPORT IRQ4 (vector 68). Peer steps the window state `+8` from 1 to `0xC` (hello "HO"/"HA" at `+0/+2`, `0xA5A5` at `+4`, window RAM test with `0xAAAAAAAA`/`0x55555555`, sample chunks), then installs its frame handler `0x40000934`. MAIN status `0x41bbf448` and state `0x41bb32b0` reach 6. Without a peer, "DSP BOOT FAILURE (TIMEOUT)" follows after `0x12` poll periods (about 1.04 G emulated instructions). `[emu]` — `syntakt#bd4d9eed` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:221](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L221) · Syntakt / digikit findings: peer CPU, RAM, card, NOR, panel (OS 1.42, static and emulator, 2026-11-18)
- [doc] [emu] MAIN mixes the digital voices and owns the audio clock: eDMA ch 54 (TCD `0xFC0456C0`) streams a 2 KB ring at SRAM `0x80000000` (64 frames x 8 words) to the SSI TX FIFO `0xFC0C8000`; its half-way interrupt is the 1500 Hz audio frame (32 samples at 48 kHz, SSI1 slave; vector 174, handler `0x400a2058`). That handler forces INTC1 source 63 to run the engine tick (vector 191, `0x400a38ce`, 7,550 bytes), which mixes the 8 voices from `0x80003d50` in Q31 and fills the other half. Codes: 1-16 trigs, 17 FUNC, 18 TRK, 19 TRIG, 20 SYN, 21 none, 22 FLTR, 23 AMP, 24 LFO, 25 SETTINGS, 26 FX, 27 TEMPO, 28 NO, 29-31 LEFT/DOWN/RIGHT, 32 PAGE, 33 BANK, 34 PTN, 35 SONG/SOUND (three dots), 36 REC, 37 PLAY, 38 STOP, 39 YES, 40 UP, 41-48 encoder pushes G,F,E,B,A,D,C,H. - [emu] Native Bitmap API (1.42 MAIN): constructor `0x400f72be(object, width, height, pixels, mask)`, clipped rectangle fill `0x400f7fb6`, masked blit `0x400f8f70(dst, src, x, y, flags)`; an eight-word object can borrow pixel and mask arrays with no heap allocation. A 128 x 64 bitmap is 256 big-endian words per array, two words per column; y = 0 is bit 31 of the first word, y = 63 bit 0 of the second; a zero mask bit keeps the destination pixel. This is the bitmap layer; the panel's own row order is a different layer (compare D13). `[emu]` (executed in Unicorn) {synfact-1119} — `syntakt#c4d16512` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:244](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L244) · Syntakt / Upgrade receiver, transport state, native bitmaps (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18)

- [doc] [emu] Parameter locks are a full matrix, no row pool: per track `0x2447` bytes, 64 steps × 72 int16 (ids 0..70, −1 none; word 71 the step's lock count) plus 71 per-id bytes; address `locks + 0x2447·track + 2·(72·step + id)`. Set `0x40017602`, clear `0x4001741e`, get `0x4001722a` (model level, no length check); `0x40027fa2` is the track-level set that refuses steps past the length. Nothing counts rows, so the Rytm's 72-row limit does not exist here. - [emu] Stock MAIN cost (emulator profile with a calibrated cache model, default project in PLAY, not meter readings): the block routine `0x400a38ce` is 97.5 % of MAIN's instructions. Per block about 72,400 instructions, 1,466 I-cache misses and 206 D-cache misses, modelled as 77 % of a 250 MHz MAIN; stopped gives nearly the same. About 22 KB of code runs every block against an 8 KB, 4-way, 16-byte-line I-cache, so almost every hot line misses once per block: 1 KB less code per block is about 1.5 MAIN points, 1,000 fewer instructions about 0.5. The model (cycles ~ 0.85 x instructions + 40 x misses) was fitted on a unit for AUDIO code and predicted the first Chorus port's jump from 88 % to 100 %. `[emu]` — `syntakt#7099c448` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:271](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L271) · Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)

With an 8 KB I-cache against about 22 KB of code per block, any lock set covers at most about 16-19 %, so a better lock set than icache-lock-st's cannot recover much. The MAIN parameter smoother keeps its arrays in SRAM (uncached) and runs with `MACSR=0x28`; its one-pole has a history-dependent dead band, so "converged" is not one value. - [emu] digikit's card write guard (built for the Syntakt, emulator only): `before` hooks at both entries refuse a request outside the row of its writer class (stock: `[0, 0x180000)`; the runtime's own write, known by its return address: the store) and return -10, the driver's own out-of-range code, before any lock is taken. The Data API then reports "Failed to write to eMMC". It cannot see the finale's raw writes or CMD6. The guard is on in both Syntakt sets; no refusal was reported from the unit. `[emu]` (SB35) — `syntakt#fa0c5b4c` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:299](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L299) · Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)

- [doc] What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re} — `firmware-container#ded70082` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:61](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L61) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)

- [doc] Syntakt (SyntHack OS `RECOVERY.md`): if the OS still boots, flash the stock `.syx` via Transfer's Drop page (works even if a mod misbehaved); if not, MIDI interface with a 5-pin OUT to the Syntakt's MIDI IN ("USB doesn't work from the startup menu"), FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4, Transfer SYSEX TRANSFER "OS Upgrade via device startup menu", tens of minutes at 31.25 kbit/s, the unit restarts itself. Avoid TRIG 2 (empty reset) and TRIG 3 (factory reset) in the startup menu - both erase data. Do a dry run of the DIN procedure with the stock OS before the first flash; flash only files for which `tools/unpack/eft.py info <file>` reports `checksums : ok`; no hardware results are reported on the page. `[doc]` {synthack-recovery} — `recovery#2934ea2d` [hardware/common/recovery.md:36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L36) · Recovery and flashing / Additions from the "read everything" pass (2026-10-31)

- [doc] Stock public Machine IDs are 0-44, stored as a BYTE in each track's machine payload (`P[t]+0xA2`); runtime records `R[t] = model + 0x6C + 0x3C0*t`, `P[t] = *(R[t]+0x10)`; the setter is at `0x40025594` (store at `0x40025620`). 505 parameter descriptors of 52 bytes; only MAIN digital tracks 0-7. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff} — `syntakt#86553c61` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L32) · Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
- [doc] Section 7 selector: a signed BYTE with a 46-entry map (negative -> 0, 0-45 kept, above 45 clamped to 45); stock maps 0-7 to the same-numbered engine family and 36->8, 37->9, 38->10, 44->11, everything else (incl. 45) to family 0. Stock tables: render pointers `0x400148F0` (12 entries), prep pointers `0x40014920`, the 46-byte map at `0x40014950`. A compact handoff moves MAIN `[0x80002000,0x800021B0)` through a 27x16-byte eDMA transfer (TCD47, channel 47); each track then receives a 20-byte copy into `T[t] = 0x80003C40 + 0x8E*t`. Dslot is 8 x `0x708` = 14,400 bytes. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff} — `syntakt#0efd67de` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:33](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L33) · Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)
- [doc] Persistence confirmed statically: the current-kit Sound-v7 save/load keeps the machine byte (raw 0-45 and 255 retained, 46-254 map to 0); Pattern-v11 stores the byte at row `+0x2EC` and its restoration is not closed; Sound locks, p-locks, held trigs, migration, clipboard and undo not qualified. Evidence labels in that repo: confirmed by static analysis / verified in emulator (none for the whole device) / verified on hardware (none) / hypothesis. `[doc]` {machine45-handoff} — `syntakt#899e0c2a` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:34](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L34) · Syntakt / Syntakt OS 1.41 static-analysis facts (Humgic/syntakt-machine45-research - README and handoff dated 2026-10-28; no hardware run, no firmware)

- [doc] Two ColdFire MCF5441x (V4, EMAC, no FPU, ~250 MHz, so 166,667 cycles per 32-sample block), with 64 KB SRAM at `0x80000000`. RAM shared between the CPUs is at `0x10000000`. `[doc]` — `syntakt#9f88239a` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:38](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L38) · Syntakt / Platform: two ColdFires, an FPGA, an analog mixer (SyntHack OS docs, OS 1.41)
- [doc] Boot: entry `0x400004E8`; static constructors loop `0x40082500` (136 entries); the intro animation task `0x40087E6A` gates boot, so never make the intro longer. Screen: 128x64 1 bpp, column-major, double buffer at `0x402D6DC4`/`0x402D6DC0`; frame loop `0x4000A0E6` redraws when `*(0x444E1334)+96` is set. `[doc]` — `syntakt#3245b484` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:73](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L73) · Syntakt / Memory map of CPU #1 (OS 1.41)
- [doc] CPU #2 (section 7): all work runs in the audio interrupt `0x40000934` (vector 96, DMA timer 0 capture). Per block it copies `0x1B0` bytes of parameters from shared RAM and renders 8 digital voices (`0x40004324`). It returns 8 x 32 int32 over eDMA channel 47 and does no mixing. 12 engines: tables at `0x400148F0` (render), `0x40014920` (update), `0x40014950` (machine id -> engine). Order: BD MODERN, SD BASIC, CY ALLOY, PC CARBON, SY TONE, SY CHORD, SD VINTAGE, CP VINTAGE, SY TOY, SY BITS, SY SWARM, SP TWINSHOT. SY CHORD reads a 512 x int32 wave at `0x4001A300`. `[doc]` — `syntakt#3d42d4e8` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:76](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L76) · Syntakt / Audio path
- [doc] CPU #1 (section 3): the per-block routine `0x400A3856` runs CV/gain, ADC deinterleave, then master/FX `0x4008F1CA`. Delay `0x40096890` and reverb `0x40096E3C` are the same code as on the Digitakt mk1. Buffers: digital tracks from CPU #2 at `0x80003D50`. ADC channels at `0x80003950`: 0-3 analog tracks, 4-5 external in, 6-7 the FX-track bus. USB/Overbridge: 20 channels per frame at `0x80004760`. The final mix is analog: digital buses go out through DACs into an analog mixer, with nothing digital after them. 40 control voltages go out over DSPI1 with eDMA channel 15; CV 35/36 are the FX-track bus VCAs. `[doc]` — `syntakt#9e1d0250` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:80](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L80) · Syntakt / Audio path
- [doc] Section 7 is byte-identical in 1.41 and 1.42 (SHA-256 `daf6451c...783bc2`). It is ColdFire ISA-C with EMAC, MCF5441x-class: compile with `-mcpu=54418`, disassemble with `-m m68k:isa-c:emac`. CPU #2 has its own 128 MB SDRAM at `0x40000000` (SP `0x48000000`, entry `0x40001070`). `[doc]` — `syntakt#e773fe40` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:89](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L89) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] Only 39.8 KB is code (`0x40000404-0x40009f88`: boot, audio interrupt, voice loop, 12 engines, sample loader), followed by 284 KB of tables and data. Code room for mods is almost nil: ~318 bytes in small pieces remained after SynCrackd's images. — `syntakt#e1ec1d13` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:90](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L90) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] The sample pool is in CPU #2's RAM: 64 MB from `0x4004f750`, in BSS zeroed at boot. A 64-entry slot table `{u32 frames, u32 pointer}` is at `0x4404f754`. Format: 64 times `u32 frames` + big-endian int16 mono. The main CPU fills it at boot in 2 KB chunks through the shared window `0x800`, with an unchecked 16-bit index. This is the slow boot the manual mentions. Per slot at most 524,287 frames (10.9 s; positions are 20.12 fixed point). The stock UI limits slots to 5 s and "32 MB". — `syntakt#7abf02d7` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:92](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L92) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] Shared window (CPU #2 `0x0-0x1000` = main CPU `0x10000000`, chip select 0, 16-bit, one wait state): `0x000-0x1b0`: the parameter block, copied to `0x80008000` every block; `0x1b0-0x5b0`: 8 mono track buffers, sent by eDMA 47; `0x5b0-0x800`: unused by stock; `0x800-0x1000`: the sample chunk at boot. — `syntakt#584bee6c` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:97](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L97) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`
- [doc] SRAM `0x80000000`: 8 voices of 1,800 B, 8 mono int32 output buffers, 8 parameter blocks of 142 B. The highest static reference is `0x8000f670`, so treat SRAM as full. — `syntakt#e90b2942` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:102](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L102) · Syntakt / CPU #2 (the voice CPU, section 7) - memory map from SynCrackd (OS 1.41 and 1.42) `[doc]`

- [doc] Each change is stored with the SHA-256 of the original bytes, so a different OS version fails the build instead of crashing. Every mod runs in a Unicorn emulator next to the original code before flashing. Stock Unicorn gets signed fractional EMAC wrong (the audio comes out silent), so EMAC instructions are trapped and executed in Python from the NXP manual. Use CPU model "ANY" (the code needs FF1, MVS/MVZ, SATS). — `syntakt#1144e802` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:110](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L110) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
- [doc] Hooks: replace at least 6 bytes with `jsr` plus `nop` padding, and the trampoline replays the replaced instructions. Save every register; replay replaced EMAC instructions first. If your code uses EMAC, set MACSR yourself and leave ACC0 at 0, because the OS sum routines start from it. One-time setup goes in a hook in the page initializer (`0x401885D2...`), never in boot time. — `syntakt#d4c263b4` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:113](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L113) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
- [doc] Mod code: gcc/as with `-mcpu=54418`, no `.bss` (put variables in `.data`), no libgcc (`nm -u` empty). ColdFire limits: `muls.l` takes no absolute address, there is no `exg`, `movem` takes only `(An)`/`d16(An)`, short branches reach ±127 B. — `syntakt#56340605` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:117](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L117) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
- [doc] Spare storage the OS saves without knowing: per track: engine word +106 (hidden id 72); per kit: unused words of the pattern kit at `*0x800030BC` (ids 0, 0x1A, 0x24, 0x27, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x37, 0x46, 0x38). Store values XOR their default, so old projects load with defaults; kit words 41-43 of the 12 per-track kit blocks (Digitakt MIDI-track data, unused here); 256 bytes in the project settings file. A "free" parameter id can be an alias the OS shows in some modes, so audit it. — `syntakt#fee3a98a` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:119](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L119) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
- [doc] UI internals: parameter descriptors at `0x4022D59C + 52*id`; page objects at `0x41B9F3C8` (44 B, 8 slots); per-parameter `std::function` objects at `0x41B9FA24 + 84*id` (+20 text, +36 icon, +68 style). Page 25 ("OB8") is a free Digitakt leftover. Rewrite a `std::function` only from UI code, never from the audio interrupt. — `syntakt#71876d6e` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:125](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L125) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`
- [doc] Audio mods: Hook the mix function; keep the OS's EMAC `msac` sign convention (the result is -Σ g·x). Do nothing when there is nothing to do. Compute at 24 kHz where the sound allows it. Ramps must snap to their target or the effect never goes idle. Limit how far a modulated delay moves per block. Keep a cost-per-block regression test (count instructions with `UC_HOOK_CODE` after `ctl_flush_tb()`). — `syntakt#33df5f9d` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:126](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L126) · Syntakt / How mods are built on the Syntakt (SyntHack modding guide, worth copying) `[doc]`

- [doc] The analog tracks reuse the Analog Rytm MKII's voice design. The voice control records have the Rytm MKII's format (command/depth word, start and target bytes, mode nibble, rate exponent and mantissa). The cymbal oscillator banks use the Rytm's scale (43.62 units per Hz) and load the Rytm's CH/CB CLASSIC values. So Rytm voice research applies here and back. `[doc]` (inferred from the shared formats) — `syntakt#61c6c351` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:156](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L156) · Syntakt / What the Syntakt shares with other boxes (merged from analog-emu's Syntakt port, OS 1.42, static plus emulator)
- [doc] Bank store: two 8 MiB slots inside the old 16 MiB `/mods` reservation, metadata sectors at eMMC `0x02bffe00` and `0x033ffe00`; the legacy record at `0x03400000` is still read. `[doc]` — `syntakt#141be7f1` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:164](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L164) · Syntakt / Synfact core and SMZ4 banks (OS 1.41, 2026-11-10)
- [?] [doc] Safe boot: a bank moves CANDIDATE -> TRYING (written before any bank code runs) -> GOOD, set once AUDIO and the sample pool are ready and 150 UI ticks (about 5 s) have passed; a crash or power-off before that boots the previous GOOD bank or stock machines. Each bank names an exact core contract, and the core checks the stock bytes that LFO3 and MODULATION SKIP patch before any initializer runs. `[doc]`, rollback `[?]` (not yet tested on hardware). - [doc] Nothing in the stock AUDIO image names an address above `0x4404f980` (the end of the zeroed data, named once by the clear; no allocator). The AUDIO stack starts at `0x48000000`, the main context idles and all work runs in the block interrupt: at most 3,140 bytes deep by static count. ACR0 `0x4007e020` caches `0x40000000-0x47ffffff`, so AUDIO has 128 MiB as MAIN does. - [doc] Cache control: stock MAIN has a single `movec cacr`, at boot (`0x4000055a`, value `0xa50ce100`: I- and D-cache, store buffer and branch cache on). - [doc] Native project workers (1.42 MAIN): each project command loads its worker's address with a `move.l #imm,d0` at a fixed site: new `0x4005d83a` (worker `0x40059f9e`), rename `0x4005a486` (`0x4005a6f8`), copy `0x4005a558` (`0x4005a788`), paste `0x4005a606` (`0x4005a7aa`), clear `0x4005a6a6` (`0x4005a7d0`), clear selected `0x4005d20e` (`0x4005a828`), delete selected `0x4005d3b6` (`0x4005a8a2`), save `0x4005b662` (`0x4005ba50`), load `0x4005d9dc` (`0x4005bafa`). Autosave and project SysEx do not go through them. `[doc]` — `syntakt#bf2a7dd5` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:274](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L274) · Syntakt / Synfact findings: AUDIO memory, MAIN CPU profile, project workers (OS 1.42, 2026-11-18/19)
- [doc] FX ADC pair: the detector input for the FX bus is fixed at `0x80003c50` and `0x80003cd0`, 32 signed Q31 frames each (the ADC 6/7 capture SyntHack named on 1.41). `[doc]` — `syntakt#4e9590f6` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:279](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L279) · Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
- [doc] The digital FX bus is not the whole FX input: `0x8000dad0` (Synfact's `ST_FX_TRACK_BUS`, the first of the six mixer buses) is the digital bus before the analog FX block. Processing it digitally does not cover what the analog circuit routes to FX; for that, detect on the ADC pair and act on the VCAs. `[doc]` — `syntakt#368f0fd3` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:280](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L280) · Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
- [doc] Kit pointers and codecs on 1.42: live kits at `0x41ad6134 + k*0x1618`, k < 128 (1.41: `0x41ad5134`, the `+0x1000` DDR shift). `KitActive::kitChanged` is `0x40172414` (vtable `0x401c3694` +`0x5c`; object `0x40a713f0`, kits at its +`0x10`). Native Kit new `0x400b3384`, encode `0x400a78f4`, decode `0x400a78a0`; native memcpy `0x4011613c`; the global Kit model's has/get/set start at `0x4000d870`, `0x4000d94a`, `0x4000da32`. Core 2.4 takes these sites once and passes notifications to modules, so Chorus and LFO3 no longer patch them themselves. `[doc]` — `syntakt#b05cfa89` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:281](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L281) · Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
- [doc] Kit slot tail, 1.42: native `[0, 0x14d2)`, LFO3 `[0x14e0, 0x15d0)`, comp-st `[0x15d0, 0x15e0)` (tag `0x4351`, six big-endian Q8 words, a 16-bit check), playhead-st `[0x15e0, 0x15f8)`; the tail is now full up to `0x15f8`. The native Kit SysEx uses a shorter layout, so tail data does not travel in a Kit SysEx dump. `[doc]` — `syntakt#0200cbe8` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:282](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L282) · Syntakt / Synfact findings: FX-bus compressor, kit codecs, real-bank profile (OS 1.42, core 2.4.0, 2026-11-20)
- [doc] The patched image did not fit without packing section 7: Elektron stores section 7 raw (383,760 B, SHA-256 `daf6451c...ec783bc2`); with it raw the patched container was 2,129,312 B, 32,672 B over the 2 MiB upgrade limit (`0x1FFE00`). Packed (aPLib with an 8-byte header: big-endian body length and byte sum) it is 264,194 B. The full set with the guard is 2,079,872 B (16.4 KB free). `[doc]` — `syntakt#b6e74e47` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:289](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L289) · Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
- [doc] How MAIN reads section 7 (no stage buffer): the peer thread (entry `0x40082c04`, made by `0x40082e9c` from the boot thread) loads A2 with the NOR read `0x40116d7a` (6-byte `lea` at `0x40082c24`), reads id 6 into `0x4f8af2c9` and id 7 straight into the transmit buffer at `0x4f84f2c6` (`0xAA` at `0x4f84f2c1`, big-endian length at `0x4f84f2c2`). The only length check is `length + 5 <= 0x60000` at `0x40082d66` (else "DSP BOOT FAILURE (BUF)"); a missing id gives status 1 at `0x40082e84`. No other code reads id 7; the bootstrap and the OS-upgrade receiver do not parse sections. The handshake timeout (about 5.1 s, 19 polls) starts only after both NOR reads and the DMA arm, so unpacking before the stream costs no timeout time. `[doc]` — `syntakt#e59a2190` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:290](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L290) · Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
- [doc] The second CPU must get the exact stock bytes: section 7 carries a second FPGA bitstream (at `0x40041060`) that the peer loads through its own DSPI. MAIN configures the main FPGA itself from section 1: `0x400bd74e` reads id 1, unpacks it with `0x401181ec` to `0x43be315c` (length at `0x43be3158`, 149,516 B), and `0x400bcb4e` shifts it out over DSPI `0xFC03C000` after INIT goes high. This corrects the earlier "the bootstrap configures the FPGA" (section list above). `[doc]` — `syntakt#5f4af7f0` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:292](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L292) · Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
- [doc] Key ids in key events differ from the Digitakt II/Digitone II: the id at +`0xc` of a key event is the firmware key index from the decoder table `0x401d7a48`: YES 12, NO 13, RIGHT 17, LEVEL push 48 (a second YES key in lists; the stock compact menu handler `0x400f5c82` treats 12 and `0x30` alike). On DT2/DN2 the same keys are 10, 12, 15 and 49. The flag bits look the same: bit 0 set on a press (cursor keys and RIGHT act on it), bit 4 on a release (YES acts on it). `[doc]` (I181) — `syntakt#ff196a42` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:294](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L294) · Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
- [doc] The card capacity is a driver word: the eSDHC init (`0x4010ebea`, boot thread) stores the capacity in sectors at `0x444ba720` (from EXT_CSD SEC_COUNT, else the CSD); the 20-byte getter `0x4010f232` returns it, or `0xFFFFFFFF` while the driver is not ready (same hash on DT2 1.17 `0x4012ddd6`, DN2 1.12 `0x4012c49a`, DN2 1.11 `0x4012c1ba`). The part table (7 rows of 32 bytes at `0x402d5adc`) is checked at boot but not enforced on the Syntakt: only the self-test reads the result (the DT2 gates its mount on it). Only the self-test makes the pSLC (enhanced area) conversion. `[doc]` — `syntakt#0ae634b8` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:295](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L295) · Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
- [doc] The eMMC write and erase entries: block write `0x4010f7f8` `(sector, bytes, buf)` and block erase `0x4010f52a` `(sector, count)` are the only MAIN code that writes or erases the user area, except the OS-upgrade finale's raw controller writes of the COKi copies (`0x400bcf7a`) and the CMD6 EXT_CSD writes in `0x4010f3d8` (one-time-programmable card setup: never call it). The write splits requests over 64 KiB by calling itself (return address entry + `0x36`) and is bounded only by the capacity; the erase checks nothing, and a count of 0 makes the end sector `sector - 1`. Both start with 8 bytes of `lea; movem.l` (no PC-relative operand); D0, D1, A0, A1 and the flags are dead at both entries; same hash and size on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12 and 1.11. Five 1.42 callers ignore the result (the console command `0x40080646`, the COKi writer `0x400bcadc`, the Data API Clear `0x400b639a`, the COKi restore `0x400bd608` twice). `[doc]` — `syntakt#befd7f8b` [hardware/devices/syntakt.md:298](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/syntakt.md#L298) · Syntakt / digikit on a Syntakt unit: section 7 packed, bootstrap stage, key ids, card capacity, write guard (OS 1.42, 2026-11-19/21)
